task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: regression to the mean and mechanical floors
methodological_questions: Is a team's defense effect on opponent H2-H1 change stable across split-halves of games and across seasons?
How much of the H2-H1 change variance is team signal versus noise with 120 team-seasons?
How should opponent quality, score state, garbage time and regression to the mean be handled?
What reliability estimator and permutation/placebo baseline are appropriate?

historical_evidence.finding: Split-half reliability of connector quality Q_p (n=102 connectors): Pearson r=+0.215, Spearman-Brown ~0.355, ICC(player-season)=0.216 (78.4% within). Judged too low to treat as a stable scoutable trait; limited by low measurement reliability (RISK:MEASURE_RELIABILITY). Different construct from this question (player attribute, not team defense).

Ranked playsheet validation after a defense drops a play type >=0.25 PPP from H1 to H2: Spearman rho=-0.0639, p=0.0997, n=665 (no clear full-rank signal); BEST>AVOID pairwise Mann-Whitney p=0.004; limited by leakage, low measurement reliability, small sample; risks include drift, lookahead, measure reliability, sample size. Concerns counter-strategy choice, not team-level reliability of H2-H1 suppression.

Foul-trouble sequencing: raw lag-1 +0.204 was an artifact of free-throw share (41.8% vs 9.9%); apples-to-apples +0.049 not significant. Failure mechanism C_artifact, with confounding, base-rate and mechanical-floor risks. Relevant only as a caution about construction artifacts in PPP-type outcomes.

Possession Control Index gain over ORtg was leakage tracking DRtg (corr +0.894); the baseline omitted defense by construction (Net=ORtg-DRtg). n=120 team-seasons, OOS 2025-26 30 teams. Relevant as a caution on mechanical overlap between defense metrics and outcomes.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a half-split-derived on-off PPP gap as a stable attribute
failed_approaches.why: Low measurement reliability; within-unit half-to-half variance dominated (limited by [prior work]).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Full-rank validation of H1-to-H2 counter-strategy rankings
failed_approaches.why: Inconclusive; limited by leakage, low measurement reliability and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Raw PPP comparison including free throws
failed_approaches.why: Artifact from mismatched free-throw composition (C_artifact, confounding, mechanical floor).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Defense-proxy metric claimed to add explanatory power beyond ORtg
failed_approaches.why: Artifact: leakage component tracked DRtg and baseline omitted defense by construction ([prior work]).

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record directly tests team-level reliability of a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change.
Closely related half-split-based constructs in this project (SF-[prior work]) showed low split-half reliability and were recorded as untestable as stable traits.
H1-to-H2 defensive change analyses (SF-[prior work]) were inconclusive and flagged for leakage, drift and unreliable measurement.
PPP-style and defense-proxy outcomes in this project have been prone to construction artifacts ([prior work], SF-[prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether team-level defensive H2-H1 suppression is reliable or unreliable; no direct estimate exists.
Whether findings from player-level connector reliability transfer to team-level effects.
What the true between-team variance of H2-H1 opponent change is, or the year-over-year persistence.
own_inferences: The H2-H1 change is a difference of two noisy half-game quantities, so its reliability is probably lower than that of either half; with ~41 games per half-split (about 82 per team-season) the split-half reliability is likely low.

Opponent H2-H1 change has a mechanical negative dependence on opponent H1 level (regression to the mean) and on game script and garbage time, which could create apparent team-level persistence or erase it.
Distinguishing a defense-specific effect from the team's own offense, pace, fatigue, rotation and coaching adjustment patterns will be hard with team-season data alone.
A null on reliability is a well-powered, informative result if framed as variance-component estimation with CIs; a positive result would require a placebo/permutation null.
uncertainties: Definition of 'defense effect' on H2-H1 change (opponent-adjusted? relative to opponent's season baseline?) is not specified.
Exact per-team game counts and possession counts per half are not shown; 120 team-seasons implies 4 seasons x 30 teams, with the partial 2025-26 data possibly now complete.
Retrieved records are indirect; read_family was not used to see full text of any record.
Whether within-team-season split halves can use odd/even games without time-drift contamination is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I would have been inclined to proceed straightforwardly. [prior work] (low split-half reliability of a half-based on-off measure, inconclusive H1-to-H2 results with leakage/drift flags, and artifacts from mechanical overlap) moved me to proceed with changes: variance-component framing, opponent-adjusted and garbage-time-trimmed outcomes, pre-specified permutation null, and a pre-registered reading that a low-reliability result is an answer rather than a failure.

blocking_constraints.text: H2-H1 difference of opponent efficiency per team-season is likely very noisy; reliability may be too low to distinguish from zero or to be useful.
Only 120 team-seasons (30 teams x 4 seasons) limit year-over-year persistence tests to roughly 90 pairs (adjacent seasons, non-independent) with modest power for small correlations.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study directly tests team-level reliability of defensive effects on opponent H2-H1 change. Adjacent work suggests low reliability for half-based constructs and inconclusive results for H1-to-H2 defensive-change analyses.

risks.text: Difference scores of half-level efficiency have low reliability; split-half of games may give r near 0. Use Spearman-Brown and variance components, and report CIs.
Opponent H2-H1 change is negatively correlated with H1 level by construction; select no teams on extreme H1 or on large drops (as in SF-[prior work] triggers) and adjust for H1 level.

Opponent quality, home/away, score state, garbage time, pace, rest, injuries, and fatigue affect H2-H1; the defense effect cannot be separated from the offense's own tendencies without opponent-adjusted baselines.
Free-throw composition, end-of-half/end-of-game foul-and-intentional-foul possessions and clock effects mechanically alter H2 PPP (cf. [prior work]); exclude or standardize.
120 team-seasons; year-over-year pairs are limited (~90) and rosters change, so persistence reflects roster turnover as much as trait.
Rules, league-wide H2 scoring trends, roster/trade changes and in-season coaching changes alter team identity; odd/even game splits may mitigate within-season drift but not between-season.
Defining the defense trait with the same games used to measure the outcome creates overlap; use disjoint game sets for trait and outcome (cf. SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work]).
If defenses are labelled 'suppressors' from H2-H1 results then tested on H2-H1 results, the label is outcome-derived; labels must come from independent games.
Reliability must exceed a permutation null (shuffled team labels within season, and shuffled half labels) rather than zero alone.
Multiple metrics (PPP, eFG, TO, rebounding) and splits will inflate false positives unless one primary metric is fixed.

design.estimand: Between-team variance share (ICC / split-half reliability) of the team defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change in points per 100 possessions, after opponent-adjustment: for each game, opponent H2-H1 change minus the opponent's own expected H2-H1 change from its games against other teams. Primary secondary estimand: year-over-year correlation of that team effect for the same franchise.
design.unit: Team-season (primary reliability within season via game-level data; 120 team-seasons across 2022-23 to 2025-26), games as sub-units; regular season primary, playoffs excluded from primary due to few games and selected matchups.
design.sample: All 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular-season games (confirm 2025-26 regular season is complete, as it was from 2026-04-13). Exclude garbage-time possessions (pre-specified score margin and time threshold) and possessions at end of halves under a fixed clock rule; exclude overtime. Free-throw-trip composition standardized or modeled.
design.power: Compute before analysis: with about 82 games per team-season, simulate the expected split-half reliability under assumed true between-team SD values and the observed game-level SD of H2-H1 change; report minimum detectable ICC. For 120 team-seasons, split-half r detects about 0.25 at 80% power (alpha 0.05); year-over-year pairs (about 90, non-independent) detect about 0.30. A reliability below about 0.3 after Spearman-Brown will be defined as 'not a reliable trait'.
design.controls: Opponent offensive baseline H2-H1 (leave-one-out), opponent H1 level (for regression to the mean), home/away, rest, score state at half, pace, and game-level random effects for team and opponent in a mixed model; defense-effect estimated from games disjoint from those used to measure the outcome (odd/even split, also first-half-of-season vs second-half as a drift check).
design.falsification: (1) Permutation null: shuffle defensive team labels within season across games to build the null distribution of split-half correlation and ICC. (2) Placebo: apply the same procedure to a different split, such as Q1-to-Q2 or odd/even possessions within a half, where no halftime adjustment is expected. (3) Negative control: the same reliability of the team's own offense H2-H1 change as a comparison. (4) Check that any reliability exceeds that implied by regression-to-the-mean mechanics via simulated games with no team effect.
design.multiplicity: One primary metric (opponent points per 100 possessions H2-H1, net of opponent baseline) and one primary reliability statistic (Spearman-Brown corrected odd/even split-half correlation). Secondary metrics (eFG%, turnover rate, rebounding, YoY persistence) reported with Holm correction and labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the Spearman-Brown corrected split-half reliability is at least 0.30 with the lower 95% bootstrap CI above 0 and above the 95th percentile of the permutation null, and the placebo split and simulation-null do not show comparable reliability, and year-over-year persistence is positive in direction. Rejected if the upper 95% CI is below 0.30 and the minimum detectable effect was met. Otherwise inconclusive. Artifact if reliability disappears after garbage-time, free-throw and regression-to-the-mean adjustments or matches the placebo.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play and box-score files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons, as available on 2026-10-06, with 2025-26 complete; freeze the file snapshot, record possession-parsing code version and thresholds before analysis.
